title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
authors: N. Liu, K. Lin, J. Hewitt, A. Paranjape, M. Bevilacqua, F. Petroni, P. Liang
before: Longer context windows were assumed to mean more usable information.
problem: Nobody had checked whether models actually use the middle of a long prompt.
breakthrough: Accuracy is high when the relevant passage is at the start or end and sags badly in the middle, in a U-shaped curve.
why: It explains why stuffing everything into context underperforms good retrieval, and why reranking still matters.
next: Better long-context training and evaluation, and continued investment in retrieval.
inherits: The knowledge that context position affects whether information is used.
